    "Java 17+ will be used as the target JDK (Spring Framework 6.0 requirement).",
    "Kafka client operations will be performed using the official Apache Kafka client library compatible with the target Kafka broker version.",

technical_and_design_decisions: Java 17+ will be used as the target JDK (Spring Framework 6.0 requirement).
Kafka client operations will be performed using the official Apache Kafka client library compatible with the target Kafka broker version.

The starting offset (U2) will be stored in the stream's deployment metadata in ZooKeeper so it survives container restarts within a deployed stream but is reset/re-read on full undeploy/redeploy cycles per the TBD behavior (treat undeploy/redeploy as a fresh deployment that respects the configured start offset).
Partition pre-allocation for Kafka source modules (U3) will use a static assignment strategy computed at deployment time, distributed evenly across the source module instances.

Message bus partition pre-allocation (U4) will follow the same static assignment pattern using the existing Spring XD message bus abstraction (Kafka/Redis/RabbitMQ transport), so that rebalancing does not occur on container crash.

The reactor-stream processor module (U6) will be built on Project Reactor, implementing time-window aggregation using Reactor's window/buffer operators with pluggable aggregate expressions (min, avg, count, sum).

Microbatching (U7) will be implemented as a buffering decorator at the source connector level, controlled by a batchInterval option that flushes a MessageBatch when the timer elapses or a size threshold is reached.
U5 is scoped as a research/POC activity (not a production feature); the deliverable is a design document and a working prototype running a sample XD stream through Spark Streaming.
U1 documentation will be written in the project's existing wiki (Confluence-style) using AsciiDoc/Markdown, including configuration reference, examples, and architecture notes.
U8 will set up an isolated rackspace environment for repeatable performance benchmarks, with scripts to reset state between runs.
assumptions: A single experienced Java/Spring developer performs all the work; estimates are pure effort (work-hours), not calendar time.
The Spring XD codebase is available and the developer is familiar with it; no ramp-up/onboarding time is included.
A test Kafka cluster, message bus broker, and ZooKeeper ensemble are available for development and integration testing.
The rackspace account (U8) is already provisioned and accessible; only setup, configuration, and benchmarking scripts are in scope.
U5 is an investigation and POC; full Spark integration into Spring XD is out of scope for this increment.
The TBD question in U2 is resolved by treating undeploy/redeploy as starting the stream from the configured offset (consuming the requirement literally).
All new modules (U6, U7) follow existing Spring XD module conventions (source/processor/sink SPI).
Documentation in U1 is incremental and covers only the new modules and features delivered in this increment.
No production hardening, security review, or operational runbook work is included beyond functional correctness and basic integration tests.

activities.activity_description: Author wiki pages documenting the new Kafka source options (starting offset, partition pre-allocation), the new message bus partition pre-allocation behavior, the reactor-stream processor module, the microbatch source option, and the performance testing setup. Includes configuration references and usage examples.

Design and implement the configuration mechanism for specifying a Kafka source starting offset (e.g., earliest, latest, or specific offset) at stream deployment. Persist the offset in stream deployment metadata so progress survives module crashes. Implement the undeploy/redeploy behavior so the stream re-reads from the configured start offset. Includes unit and integration tests.

Design and implement a static partition assignment strategy that pre-allocates Kafka topic partitions across Kafka source module instances at deployment time, eliminating the runtime rebalance step. Includes assignment algorithm, module-level partition wiring, and integration tests verifying no rebalance occurs under normal operation.

Extend the Spring XD message bus abstraction to pre-allocate transport-level partitions across nodes at stream deployment so that container crashes and redeploys do not trigger rebalancing. Includes design of the pre-allocation contract, implementation in the Kafka/Redis/RabbitMQ transports, and integration tests for crash and redeploy scenarios.

Research Spark Streaming's API surface relevant to Spring XD's data pipeline model. Build a proof-of-concept that ingests from a Spring XD source and processes the stream through Spark. Produce a design document covering architecture, integration points, and trade-offs. No production implementation.

activities.activity_name: Reactor-stream processor module with time-window operations (U6)
activities.activity_description: Implement a new XD processor module backed by Project Reactor. Support --timeWindow=<duration>, --field=<spel>, and --expressions=<list> options to compute aggregate operations (min, avg, count, sum) over time-windowed payloads. Includes SPI wiring, Reactor pipeline implementation, configuration parsing, and unit/integration tests for the example pipelines in the user story.

Add a --batchInterval=<duration> option that buffers outgoing messages and flushes them as a MessageBatch on the configured interval. Implement the buffering behavior in the source module pipeline and ensure ordering and back-pressure are preserved. Includes testing the 'http --batchInterval=10 | log' example.

Provision and configure the rackspace environment for performance testing, including Kafka cluster, message bus, and XD runtime nodes. Establish a baseline benchmark for Kafka throughput/latency. Add benchmarking scripts for the new XD use-cases (Kafka source with starting offset, partition pre-allocation, reactor-stream, microbatch). Include repeatable run scripts that reset state.

Build integrated test scenarios that combine the new features (e.g., pre-allocated Kafka source with starting offset feeding the reactor-stream module with microbatch source). Verify stream lifecycle, crash recovery, and redeploy behavior across the full pipeline.

activities.activity_name: Defect fixing, code review, and polish
activities.activity_description: Address issues found during self-review and integration testing across the increment. Includes minor refactoring, logging improvements, and final cleanup of the new modules and configuration options.
